     7→
     8→# Feature Brief — optimize-document-serializer
     9→
    10→## Summary
    11→Optimize `DocumentSerializer.SchemaSerializer.deserialize()` to reduce the 34% scan CPU cost identified by profiling. Three changes: (1) avoid the per-document `segment.toArray()` copy by using `heapBase()` for heap-backed segments with a fallback path for off-heap/mmap'd/remote segments, (2) precompute schema-derived constants (boolCount, mask byte sizes, field-is-boolean flags, field list as array) in the `SchemaSerializer` constructor instead of recomputing per document, (3) replace the per-field `switch` pattern matching in `decodeField` with a precomputed field decoder dispatch table. Target: ~10-12% scan CPU reduction.
    12→
    13→## Actors
    14→- `DocumentSerializer.SchemaSerializer` — the inner class implementing `MemorySerializer<JlsmDocument>`
    15→- `DocumentSerializer` — static utility methods for field encoding/decoding
    16→
    17→## Inputs
    18→- `MemorySegment` containing serialized document bytes (heap-backed, off-heap, or remote-backed)
    19→- `JlsmSchema` defining field types and order (fixed per serializer instance)
    20→
    21→## Outputs / Side Effects
    22→- `JlsmDocument` with deserialized field values — identical output to current implementation
    23→- No change to serialization (encode) path
    24→- No change to the binary format
    25→
    26→## Business Rules
    27→- Heap-backed segments (`heapBase().isPresent()`) use the backing array directly with offset — zero-copy
    28→- Off-heap segments (mmap'd, remote) fall back to `toArray()` copy — correct but not zero-copy
    29→- Schema constants computed once in `SchemaSerializer` constructor, not per `deserialize()` call
    30→- Field decoder dispatch table built once per schema, indexed by field position
    31→- Deserialization must produce byte-identical results to the current implementation for all field types
    32→- Schema evolution (write-time field count < current field count) must still work correctly
    33→
    34→## Error Cases
    35→- Corrupt data: same behavior as current — `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` or malformed VarInt propagates as-is
    36→- Off-heap segment with insufficient length: same as current — bounds check by MemorySegment API
    37→
    38→## Explicit Out of Scope
    39→- Serialization (encode) path optimization
    40→- Lazy field deserialization (deferring String construction until `getString()` is called)
    41→- Primitive boxing elimination (requires `JlsmDocument` model redesign)
    42→- Binary format changes
    43→- SIMD acceleration of scalar field decoding (already used for array types)
    44→
    45→## Acceptance Criteria
    46→1. All existing `DocumentSerializer` and `JlsmTable` tests pass — byte-for-byte identical deserialization
    47→2. `heapBase()` fast path avoids `toArray()` allocation for heap-backed segments
    48→3. Off-heap/mmap'd segments fall back correctly to `toArray()` copy
    49→4. `countBoolFieldsUpTo()` is not called during deserialization — constants precomputed
    50→5. Field decoding uses dispatch table instead of `switch` pattern matching
    51→6. Perf-review scratch benchmark shows measurable scan throughput improvement
    52→
    53→## Open Assumptions
    54→- The JIT compiler does not already optimize away the `toArray()` copy for heap-backed segments (profiler evidence suggests it does not — 103 samples in copy frames)
    55→- Field decoder dispatch table via `@FunctionalInterface` lambdas will inline well under JIT — needs benchmark validation
    56→- Off-heap segment fallback path performance is acceptable (same as current behavior)
    57→
    58→## Performance Expectations
    59→- Baseline: DocumentSerializer deserialization = 34% of scan CPU (432 profiler samples)
    60→- Target: ~10-12% reduction in deserialization CPU
    61→  - `toArray()` elimination: ~8% (103 samples)
    62→  - Schema constant precomputation: ~1.5% (19 samples)
    63→  - Dispatch table: ~1-2% estimated
    64→- Validation: perf-review scratch benchmark comparing scan throughput before/after
    65→
    66→## Project Context
    67→- Language: Java 25 (Amazon Corretto)
    68→- Framework: none — pure library
    69→- Test framework: JUnit Jupiter (JUnit 5)
    70→

     6→
     7→# Domain Analysis — optimize-document-serializer
     8→
     9→## Overview
    10→This feature optimizes the internal deserialization path of an existing class
    11→(`DocumentSerializer.SchemaSerializer`). No APIs, formats, or module boundaries
    12→change. The optimization targets are identified by profiler evidence and operate
    13→within well-defined JDK FFM API semantics and the existing binary format.
    14→
    15→## Domains
    16→
    17→### MemorySegment Heap Access
    18→**Status:** resolved
    19→**Relevance:** The zero-copy fast path uses `MemorySegment.heapBase()` and
    20→`heapOffset()` to access the backing byte[] directly. The semantics are defined
    21→by the JDK FFM API.
    22→
    23→**Guidance for implementation:**
    24→- `heapBase()` returns `Optional<Object>` — present for heap-backed segments
    25→  (`MemorySegment.ofArray(byte[])`), empty for off-heap (mmap, Arena-allocated)
    26→- Cast `heapBase().get()` to `byte[]` for heap segments; use `(int) heapOffset()`
    27→  as the array start offset (may be non-zero for sliced segments)
    28→- Off-heap fallback: `segment.toArray(ValueLayout.JAVA_BYTE)` — same as current behavior
    29→
    30→---
    31→
    32→### DocumentSerializer Binary Format
    33→**Status:** resolved
    34→**Relevance:** The brief explicitly constrains this feature to preserve the
    35→existing binary format. No format changes, no version bumps.
    36→
    37→**Guidance for implementation:**
    38→- All three optimizations (heap access, precomputed constants, dispatch table)
    39→  are internal to the `deserialize()` method — the wire format is unchanged
    40→- Round-trip tests (serialize → deserialize) must produce identical results
    41→- Schema evolution (write-time field count < current) must still work
    42→
    43→---
    44→
    45→## Unresolved Gaps
    46→None.
    47→
    48→## Key Constraints for Implementation
    49→- `heapBase()` fast path must have a correct fallback for off-heap segments
    50→- Schema constants (boolCount, mask sizes, field flags) computed once in constructor
    51→- Field decoder dispatch table indexed by field position, built per schema
    52→- Binary format is unchanged — all existing tests must pass identically
    53→- No changes to the serialization (encode) path
